message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The financial picture is solid: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), gross margin of $180.7 billion (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%), and operating income of $123.2 billion. Net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down slightly year over year, but only because of a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid ruling — operating performance actually improved, and cash generated by operating activities was a robust $118.3 billion against $9.4 billion of capex. Services revenue grew 13% to $96.2 billion at a 73.9% gross margin, giving the franchise a durable, high-margin growth engine, while the balance sheet holds $140.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. Growth is modest (iPhone flat, Greater China down 8%) and there are real regulatory overhangs (DOJ antitrust suit, DMA proceedings with fines of up to 10% of worldwide sales), which argued for a measured position rather than a large one. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single limit buy order for 44 shares at $222.85 — about $9,805, under the $10,000 per-order cap and about half of the $20,000 daily allowance, with $50,000 of cash available and no money moved out of the account. The order filled at $222.85. (Note: my first submission was rejected before execution because I included an unsupported "gross margin" field; I resubmitted with only verified income-statement and cash-flow figures and it filled.)
